starting_points.name: Cargo binary package
starting_points.when: A new Rust CLI needs a new directory.
steps: Install the chosen Rust toolchain. Replace /path/to/workspace with the actual local source parent; choose the real package name.
Generate a binary package; use --lib only for a reusable library rather than an executable.
notes: A Cargo package is not a full framework application. Preserve generated defaults and add only selected dependencies.

starting_points.name: Cargo in an existing directory
starting_points.when: An existing source directory has no Cargo.toml and must become a package; choose this instead of cargo new.
steps: Inspect existing files and parent VCS before initialization; preserve existing code.

commands.purpose: Initialize a binary package in place.

notes: Use --lib for a library target. Do not run cargo init over an already initialized package.

starting_points.name: Ratatui maintained templates
starting_points.when: Interactive terminal UI is selected at project creation; use this alternative to the plain Cargo starter, rather than overlaying a template onto an existing app.
steps: Install the selected Rust toolchain; set CARGO_GENERATE_VERSION to a chosen published version and ensure Cargo binaries are on PATH.
Run the maintained template selector from the intended parent. Choose the simplest suitable template and real app name; record template choice, resolved repository revision and answers.
Review generated dependencies, license and terminal setup before extending the application.

commands.run: cargo install cargo-generate --version "${CARGO_GENERATE_VERSION:?Set the selected cargo-generate version}" --locked

commands.cwd: /path/to/workspace (parent of the new app; Git available)
commands.purpose: Choose and generate a maintained Ratatui template interactively.

notes: These are Ratatui-maintained templates, not a universal Rust CLI scaffold. Their shape depends on the selected template; resolve and retain its revision for repeatability.
Preserve terminal restoration and error/panic handling; add clap only when the generated template does not already satisfy argument parsing.

follow_up_generators.name: dist release setup
follow_up_generators.when: Only when dist is selected for shipping binaries and no equivalent release owner exists.

commands.run: cargo install cargo-dist --version "${DIST_VERSION:?Set the selected dist package version}" --locked
commands.purpose: Install the selected dist release from its cargo-dist package.
Generate release settings and selected CI.

notes: Set DIST_VERSION to a chosen published version; ensure Cargo binaries are on PATH. Review target list, metadata, installers, hooks and generated CI before adopting it.
Release configuration generation does not publish. Test each supported target and installer separately.

follow_up_generators.name: SQLx migrations and checked-query metadata
follow_up_generators.when: Only when SQLx is selected and owns schema migrations; metadata applies when checked query macros are used.

commands.cwd: /path/to/workspace/project (DATABASE_URL targets a disposable database; migration SQL reviewed)
commands.purpose: Apply migrations to the disposable database.

commands.cwd: /path/to/workspace/project (checked query macros and matching disposable schema available)

notes: Install a selected sqlx-cli release compatible with the application and selected database/TLS features. Set DATABASE_URL through the environment or an untracked local file.
Preserve migrations and commit .sqlx metadata for offline builds. Run cargo sqlx prepare --check after changes; pass workspace/feature/target options matching the project.

preserve: Preserve Cargo.toml, generated source structure and Cargo.lock after dependency resolution for shipped applications. Record the chosen Rust toolchain and generator versions.

Retain the VCS ignore baseline when generated, including build-output exclusions, and add project-specific OS metadata/secret rules. Cargo VCS behavior depends on parent repository and configuration; inspect actual output.
Record and justify changes from the same-version generator baseline instead of recreating its files from memory.
Preserve selected Ratatui template structure, terminal cleanup and license notices; keep generated dist configuration and reviewed CI synchronized.
verification: In the actual application, compare a fresh output from the recorded toolchain/options with the initial project and explain intentional differences.
After initial dependency resolution, run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --locked and cargo build --locked from the package root; run the project-selected Clippy checks.
In a disposable copy, inspect git add --dry-run -A and confirm source/manifests/lockfile are included while target/, credentials and .DS_Store are excluded.
Test command help, exit codes, piped input/output, interruption and terminal restoration; a successful build is not proof of terminal behavior.

sources.title: dist release setup and generated CI

integration_steps: After the selected Cargo or Ratatui template baseline, add typed clap arguments when needed with cargo add clap --features derive; preserve equivalent argument parsing already supplied by the chosen template.

Resolve Ratatui and its supported terminal backend only when interactive rendering is required; preserve the selected template's compatible setup. Add reqwest only when network access is needed, deliberately selecting blocking or async behavior.
Implement typed commands, validated settings, stable output/exit codes and domain logic independent of terminal rendering; propagate cancellation and support non-TTY consumers.
Add executable behavior tests with cargo add --dev assert_cmd; cover missing files, invalid input, stdin, cancellation, stdout/stderr and terminal cleanup. Run the profile verification checks.

When dist is selected, follow its release generator instructions and review target list and generated CI. Lock dependencies/toolchain, qualify native dependencies and installers, and preserve Cargo.lock. No application setup, release tags or publication were executed.
